:::{#def-quasi-newton-method}
#### Quasi-Newton method

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ have first [partial derivatives](vector-calculus.qmd#def-partial-derivative),
let $\vx^{(0)}$ be a starting point,
and let $\matr{H}^{(0)}$ be a [positive definite matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite).
A **quasi-Newton method**
[@nocedal2006numerical, Chapter 6]
produces, for $t = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$,

$$
\vx^{(t+1)} \eqdef \vx^{(t)} - \alpha^{(t)} \matr{H}^{(t)} \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t)}),
$$

where $\alpha^{(t)} > 0$ is a [step length](#def-gradient-descent) chosen by a [line search](#def-line-search),
and $\matr{H}^{(t+1)}$ is a [symmetric](linear-algebra.qmd#def-symmetric-matrix) positive definite matrix
whose [inverse](linear-algebra-special-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-inverse) satisfies the [secant condition](#def-secant-condition), that is,
$\matr{H}^{(t+1)} \vy^{(t)} = \vecf{s}^{(t)}$,
with $\vecf{s}^{(t)} = \vx^{(t+1)} - \vx^{(t)}$
and $\vy^{(t)} = \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t+1)}) - \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t)})$.

:::
